title: (d) a document that is not a bundle is refused with a readable reason
summary: Paste a lone `{` into the Import box and the panel refuses it with a sentence, not a stack trace. The read handler POSTs the pasted text to `/api/compositions/import` with `preview:true`; the server's `parseCompositionBundle` fails `JSON.parse` and throws a human sentence, which comes back as a 400 body and is shown verbatim in the import error alert. The refusal is decided on the server — the paste box does not parse client-side, deliberately, so the error is spoken in one voice.

states.label: Import / Export — a non-bundle is refused
states.description: The Muster Transfer tab's Import bay. The test opens the paste box, types a single `{` (a document that is not a Garrison bundle), and asks the panel to read it. The expected outcome is not a crash but a readable refusal — this flow walks from the route to the sentence the user sees.

steps.title: The /muster route is a shim onto MusterPage
steps.description: Navigating to `/muster?...&section=transfer` lands on a three-line server component that mounts `MusterPage`; the section query param selects the Transfer tab inside it, and the Transfer tab hosts the Import bay whose paste box this flow drives. There is no data-loading in the route itself.

steps.title: Open the paste box
steps.description: Click `import-paste-toggle` (the "or paste JSON" link button). It flips local `pasteOpen` state to reveal the textarea — no logic worth banding.

steps.title: Type `{` — a document that is not a bundle
steps.description: Fill the `import-paste` textarea with a lone `{`. This is the whole point of the case: a single brace is well-formed-looking but not parseable JSON and carries none of a bundle's shape. It only updates `pasteText` state.

next.label: ask the panel to read it

steps.title: Read the pasted text — the climax action
steps.description: Click `import-paste-read`. Its handler calls `accept(pasteText)`, which hands the raw string straight to `runPreview` — the paste box never parses client-side, so the `{` travels to the server as-is. This is the action under test; everything after it is how the refusal comes back.

steps.title: runPreview POSTs the raw text and catches the refusal
steps.description: `runPreview` POSTs `{ bundle: "{", preview: true }` to `/api/compositions/import` — a real server round-trip; the client does no parsing of its own. When the server answers non-2xx it throws `data.error`, and the catch writes that message into `error` state and drops back to the empty phase. Whatever readable sentence the server produced is now the user-facing reason.

next.label: where the server decides it is not a bundle

steps.title: parseCompositionBundle refuses the non-bundle with a sentence
steps.description: The import route calls `parseCompositionBundle` on the pasted text — the same predicate that validates an untrusted bundle on a real import. `JSON.parse("{")` throws, and the catch replaces the raw parser error with a human sentence: "that file is not valid JSON - a composition bundle is a .garrison.json document." The route returns it as a 400 body. This is the line where the refusal is decided.

steps.title: The reason renders in the import error alert
steps.description: Back in the panel, the `error` state set by `runPreview` renders in the `import-error` alert region — "That did not work" over the server's exact sentence. The test asserts against this text, so the flow ends with a readable reason on screen and nothing written to disk.
